collection.description: Families with different beliefs all want the old grove protected, for different reasons: protect it together, or argue over why.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: Some villagers want to cut the old grove for a new canoe house. (subject) wants it protected because spirits live there. (friend) wants it protected because the birds nest there and the soil holds the hill together. Their reasons are completely different. Their aim is the same. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) and (friend) stand together at the gathering, each giving their reasons. The village agrees: the grove stays. Afterwards they argue cheerfully about whose reason was better. The canoe house is built on the beach instead.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: They argue so much about whose reason is right that the gathering loses patience. The decision is delayed a month. The grove is still saved, in the end, by a vote. (subject) and (friend) are not on speaking terms for a week.
